title: Oh Happy Day! by Jordan E. Cooper at The Public #ohhappydayplay #thep...
transcript: Oh Happy Day! is probably one of my favorite pieces I've ever seen at The Public. It's a loose riff on Noah's Ark, but in this story, the protagonist first has to confront his and his family's trauma in order to save them. Written by and starring Jordan E. Cooper with some amazing gospel music by Donald Lawrence, this is the kind of boundary-pushing, genre-bending theater that never disappoints. Despite the play's happy title, this goes deep and hits hard, unearthing some really painful memories and revelations throughout various confrontations between family members and with God. Early in the play, we find Keyshawn in a liminal space that exists somewhere between reality and the afterlife. He’s instructed by God to build a boat and save his family, which seems like a pretty confusing and bold assignment, as his family has a history of leaving him behind. But sometimes, impossible situations are the only ones that can break us open in the ways that are necessary, and what follows in this play is nothing short of a reckoning. For how much pain is in this piece, there’s actually a lot of humor. The script is poetic and heavy, but just as you're locked into a super emotional moment, something will come out of left field and completely take you with laughter. This kind of experience is what makes it so thrilling. I definitely laughed a lot, but the whole thing ended with me in tears. And I love how this is a piece that sneaks up on you, because that feels apt for something that exhibits how feelings can crop up unexpectedly when you reconnect with certain people or places. Oh Happy Day! is only running for about another week, and it's a must see, so don't sleep on it. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
